title: Notes from the Asia-Pacific region: China marks PIPL's 5th anniversary, Hong Kong clarifies AI requirements
headline: China and Hong Kong Issue New AI Compliance and Data Transfer Requirements
summary: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology introduced risk assessment and expert review requirements for AI-agent terminal devices and over-the-air software updates. Meanwhile, Hong Kong's Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data issued a generative AI framework clarifying that uploading Hong Kong personal data to overseas-hosted models constitutes a cross-border transfer.
why_it_matters: Multinational organisations operating in the region must map their generative AI tools by server location, account for strict cross-border transfer rules, and prepare for mandatory expert reviews on post-market software updates.

quotes.text: Most significantly, over-the-air upgrades are now subject to expert review.

Organizations using Hong Kong as a regional hub or preparing for a Hong Kong listing should map their generative AI tools by server location, update their privacy notices and keep records of AI data flows ready for due diligence.

dates_mentioned.what: Anhui Province branch of the Cyberspace Administration of China issued the Anhui FTZ data export negative list
dates_mentioned.quote: On 11 Nov., the Anhui Province branch of the Cyberspace Administration of China and other provincial authorities jointly issued the Anhui FTZ data export negative list, 2026 edition, and its implementing measures.

classification.significance_reason: Introduces concrete regulatory hurdles and compliance requirements for AI agents, software updates, and cross-border data transfers in major Asian jurisdictions.
